in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**What age is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- **How old is the child** (or children, if you have more than one)?
- **What are their names?** (This will help me give you a clear final answer)

The age is important because it affects eligibility:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify
- **16-19**: Need to be in full-time education or approved training
- **20 or over**: Generally don't qualify

Please share the details and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh hi, thanks for helping me with this. I've got one child - Alex, who's 20 years old. He lives at home with me here in Bristol. I was wondering if I could still claim for him?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've told me, Alex is 20 years old, which means we need to check if he falls into a category that qualifies for Child Benefit.

Let me navigate through the eligibility check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm afraid I have some bad news regarding Alex's eligibility.

**Result: INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Reason:**
Child Benefit can only be claimed for children who are:
- Under 16 years old, **OR**
- Aged 16-19 and in approved full-time education or training

Since Alex is 20 years old, he no longer qualifies, even though he lives at home with you.

**Important to know:**
- If Alex had just turned 20 and was previously receiving Child Benefit, the payments would have stopped when he reached that age
- If he's aged 16-17 and has recently left education or training, there is a 20-week extension period available if he registered with a careers service or armed services (but this doesn't apply to Alex at 20)

**Next steps:**
If you have any other children under 20 who are in education/training, I'd be happy to check their eligibility. Otherwise, if you have questions about other benefits or support Alex might be eligible for, you may want to contact:
- **HMRC Child Benefit helpline** for further guidance
- **Your local Citizens Advice** for information about other financial support

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but thank you for explaining it clearly. No, Alex is my only child, so I guess that's that then. I appreciate you taking the time to go through it with me. At least I know where I stand now. Thanks again for your help.
